baseline._about: Words the learner already knows: everyday Android and Kotlin, plus the Encryption course.

avoid._about: Words a beginner misreads or that hide who does what.

phrases.the system: name the actor: the radio, the server, the cache
phrases.just a: cut it, or say what it is

packet.def: A small chunk of data, up to about 1.5 KB, with an address on it.

IP.def: The Internet Protocol: addresses each packet and routes it, best effort.

TCP.def: Turns lost, reordered packets into a reliable, ordered stream, over a connection.

connection.def: An agreement between two sides to talk, set up before data flows, so TCP can keep its bookkeeping.

latency.def: The time a packet takes to travel from sender to receiver.

bandwidth.def: How much data a link can carry per second.

round trip.def: A message there and its answer back: twice the latency, plus the server's work.

connection reuse.def: Sending new requests over a connection that's already open, skipping its handshakes.

HTTP/2.def: A version of HTTP that sends many requests at once over one connection.

multiplexing.def: Interleaving several requests and responses on one connection at the same time.

radio state.def: The power level the phone's radio is in: idle and sipping power, or connected and drawing a lot.

tail time.def: How long the radio stays at high power after the last packet, waiting for more.

batching.def: Sending several pieces of network work together, so the radio wakes up once.

Cache-Control.def: The response header that tells a cache how long the response stays fresh.

fresh.def: A cached response young enough to use without asking the server.

ETag.def: A short tag that names one version of a resource.

conditional request.def: A request that says which version you already have; the server answers 304 if it hasn't changed.

offline-first.def: An app that reads and writes local data first, and syncs with the network when it can.

source of truth.def: The one place the app reads a piece of data from; everything else copies it.

repository.def: The class that combines the local and network data sources and gives the rest of the app its data.

idempotent.def: Doing it twice has the same effect as doing it once.

idempotency key.def: A unique ID the client sends with a request so the server can recognise a retry.

exponential backoff.def: Waiting longer after each failed try: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and so on.

jitter.def: Randomness added to the wait, so clients that failed together don't retry together.

router.def: A machine that passes data along toward its address.

connection pool.def: The set of open connections a client keeps for reuse.

3G.def: The older mobile network before LTE.

IP address.def: The number routers use to deliver packets to a machine.

hostname.def: The name code uses for a server, like api.example.com.

DNS.def: The Domain Name System: the internet's phone book, turning hostnames into IP addresses.

cached.def: Kept for a while so it doesn't have to be fetched again.

path.def: Which resource on the server a request is about, like /users/42.

header.def: A name–value pair about an HTTP message, not its data.

body.def: The data an HTTP message carries, like JSON.

status code.def: The number a response starts with; its first digit is the family: 2xx worked, 3xx elsewhere, 4xx your fault, 5xx the server's.

TLS.def: Transport Layer Security: encrypts the stream, detects changes, and proves who the server is.

certificate.def: A document, signed by an authority the phone trusts, saying a key belongs to a hostname.

handshake.def: The exchange that sets up a connection before data flows.

timeout.def: When the app stops waiting: connect timeout (no connection made) or read timeout (no answer arrived).

HTTP method.def: What a request asks for: GET reads, POST creates, PUT replaces, DELETE removes.
